insights: Technology is the most profitable category, generating $145.5K profit on $836.2K sales (17.4% margin).
Furniture is the weakest-margin category at 2.5%, despite $741.7K in sales.
Tables is a profit-draining sub-category: $207.0K sales produced -$17.7K profit (-8.6% margin).
Loss-making sub-categories overall: Tables, Bookcases, Supplies.
West is the strongest region by profit ($108.4K, 14.9% margin), while Central has the weakest regional margin at 7.9% on $501.2K sales.
Sales peaked in 2017-11 ($118.4K) and were lowest in 2014-02 ($4.5K). Fall is the strongest season by sales.
The highest monthly profit occurred in 2016-12 ($17.9K); the weakest profit month was 2015-01 (-$3.3K). Highest monthly margin: 2016-10 (27.2%).
Discounting is a material profit risk: the High (>40%) band delivered -77.4% margin versus 29.5% in the No Discount band.
Discount is negatively correlated with profit (r = -0.22), while sales and profit move together more weakly (r = 0.48).
Annual sales moved from $484.0K in 2014 to $733.2K in 2017, with profit margin 10.2% vs 12.7%.
301 products are net loss-making over the period and should be treated as portfolio risk, not merely low-volume SKUs.

recommendations.finding: Sub-categories currently destroying profit: Tables, Bookcases, Supplies.
recommendations.action: Reprice, bundle, or delist chronic loss-makers after reviewing contribution to customer baskets. Do not expand inventory in these families until margin is positive.

recommendations.finding: High (>40%) transactions produced -77.4% margin on $128.6K sales.
recommendations.action: Cap deep discounts on already-negative-margin SKUs. Require a margin floor before promotions above 20%, especially in Furniture.

recommendations.finding: 194 products combine average discount ≥ 20% with negative profit.
recommendations.action: Review list price and promotional eligibility for these SKUs. High-revenue, low-margin items should be repriced before further discounting.

recommendations.finding: 873 products sit at or below median quantity and order frequency (slow-moving candidates).
recommendations.action: Reduce replenishment on slow movers that are also low-profit. Keep inventory on high-sales/high-profit products that also move quickly.

recommendations.finding: Central has the weakest margin (7.9%); West has the strongest (14.9%).
recommendations.action: Audit mix and discounting in the weakest-margin region. Replicate assortment and pricing discipline from the strongest-margin region.

recommendations.finding: Demand and profit concentrate toward Fall; the weakest sales month in the series is 2014-02.
recommendations.action: Align working capital and promotions with the peak season rather than pushing deep discounts in already-weak months if those months also show poor margins.

recommendations.finding: Consumer contributes the most profit ($134.1K on $1.16M, 11.5% margin). Consumer has the weakest segment margin at 11.5%.
recommendations.action: Protect Consumer share in Technology. Improve mix and discount discipline for Consumer rather than chasing volume alone.
Create a monthly 'profit leak' watchlist of the worst 25 SKUs and assign owners for price, discount, or discontinuation decisions.

matrix_definitions.A. High Sales + High Profit: Core engines of the business. Protect availability, avoid unnecessary discounting, and invest in inventory and visibility.
matrix_definitions.B. High Sales + Low Profit: Revenue-rich but economically weak. These SKUs inflate the top line while consuming working capital. Immediate pricing, discount, and cost review.
matrix_definitions.C. Low Sales + High Profit: Hidden margin gems. Consider targeted marketing, better placement, or bundling to grow volume without giving away margin.
matrix_definitions.D. Low Sales + Low Profit: Candidates for rationalization. If they are also slow-moving, reduce stock or exit unless they serve a strategic basket role.
